column10: Ad-hoc parity-counting approach; had an off-by-one loop bound (excluded the all-2s case), fixed after a nudge. General dp[] tabulation version deferred to tomorrow.

notes: First formal DP lesson (5-step recipe taught from scratch - user had never learned DP theory). Naive top-down recursion correct on first try. Bottom-up tabulation had two off-by-one bugs (array sized n instead of n+1; loop stopped at i<n-1 instead of i<=n), self-found via guided tracing. Also asked a sharp conceptual question on why dp[0]=1 not 0 and understood the answer cleanly.

Start-of-session recall quiz on off-by-one-array-loop-bounds: got array size (n+1) right immediately but repeated the exact same loop-condition bug (i<n instead of i<=n) before self-correcting on one nudge - third recurrence of this bug, stayed in box 1. Main problem: needed heavy Socratic guidance to build the min-over-coins recurrence, the c<=i bounds guard (flipped it once before fixing), and the final answer/return logic (hardcoded -1, then out-of-bounds dp[n+1], then correct dp[n]). Verified working on coins=[1,2,5],n=11->3. While hand-tracing coins=[2],n=3 (expect -1) found and understood a subtler bug: per-index sentinel dp[i]=i+1 lets an unreachable dp[i-c] chain through +1 additions into a fake 'real-looking' value at a later index, so it returned 3 instead of -1. Correctly reasoned toward the fix (single global n+1 sentinel for the whole table, not i+1 per index) but session ended before re-implementing/re-testing it - resuming tomorrow.
